title: An algorithmic Ahlswede–Körner lemma
formal: Is there a constant \(a>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 2\) and all finite binary strings x,y,z with \(C(x,y)\le n\), some finite binary string \(z'\) satisfies \(C(z' |x,y)\le a \log _{2} n\) and |\(C(w|z)- C(w|z' )|\le a \log _{2} n\) for each \(w\in \{x,y,\langle x,y\rangle\}\)?
why: Tests how far a central information-theoretic replacement principle extends to individual strings, including highly non-stochastic data. Preserving the whole two-string conditional profile would clarify which information relationships can be represented by side information determined almost entirely by the data itself.
status_note: Primary formulation recovered and subsequent-work searches checked through 11 September 2026; no matching resolution located. The 2025 MFCS paper on halving algorithmic information concerns different conditional scaling requirements. General proofs were not independently verified.

progress.text: Q10 poses the general logarithmic-precision existence question; the following paragraph records a positive result under a stochastic-pair promise.
Romashchenko discusses one-shot common-information analogues in a later seminar. The checked abstract does not claim a solution to the general string problem.

sentences: For individual binary strings x and y, side information z can shorten descriptions of either string and of their pair.
The question asks whether another string \(z'\) can preserve those three conditional description lengths to logarithmic accuracy.
The replacement must have a logarithmically short description when x and y are both given.
It need not be easy to obtain from z, and no fast construction is required.
The source establishes a special case for stochastic pairs, while the general question tests the scope of an algorithmic analogue of the Ahlswede–Körner lemma.

definitions: Fix an optimal plain conditional universal machine U. Define \(C(u|v)=\min\){|\(p|:U(p,v)\) halts with output u}; there is no prefix-free restriction or time bound on programs p. Set \(C(u)=C(u|\varepsilon )\), where \(\varepsilon\) is the empty string. Use the computable, uniquely decodable pairing \(\langle x,y\rangle =1^{|}x|0xy\), and write \(C(x,y)=C(\langle x,y\rangle )\) and \(C(u|x,y)=C(u|\langle x,y\rangle )\). The integer n bounds joint description length, not the bit lengths of x or y; z has no length or complexity bound. The single constant a may depend on U and the fixed encoding, but not on n,x,y,z. Choosing a larger constant absorbs the additive effects of different fixed optimal machines or computable tuple encodings. The auxiliary string \(z'\) may depend on all three strings. No bound on \(C(z' |z)\), and no efficient procedure for finding \(z'\), is required.
answer_criterion: Prove the uniformly logarithmic bounds for every permitted triple, or refute them by showing that every constant a fails for some n,x,y,z with \(C(x,y)\le n\). An example that only violates a particular small constant does not refute the asymptotic assertion.

context_blocks.title: Replacing side information
context_blocks.text: C(x|z) measures how many program bits still describe x when z is already available. The question asks whether one can replace z while preserving the remaining description lengths of x, of y and of their pair. The replacement must itself have a short description when the pair is given.

context_blocks.title: What the replacement must preserve
context_blocks.text: The three quantities impose more than separate compression of x and y. They also constrain how much information remains shared between them. For example, when z is empty, taking \(z'\) empty satisfies the preservation requirements and makes \(z'\) describable by a fixed program.

context_blocks.title: An existence question for individual data
context_blocks.text: The algorithmic statement concerns fixed strings rather than repeated samples of random variables. The source reports the assertion for stochastic pairs: pairs that have almost maximal complexity inside a simply describable finite set. That promise is absent from the general question.

context_blocks.title: The auxiliary information need not come from z
context_blocks.text: Requiring a short program for \(z'\) given z would impose an additional common-information extraction condition. Q10 explicitly omits it. Its accompanying runtime question is separate from whether a suitable replacement exists.
